evals.prompt: I'm working in a Nuxt 4 project that already has UI Thing initialized (ui-thing.config.ts, components in app/components/Ui). Build a profile settings form with full name, email, role (Admin, Editor, Viewer) and a newsletter opt-in. Validate it, show a loading state while saving, and tell the user when it saved.
evals.expected_output: A Vue SFC using UiVee* fields inside a form with useForm and toTypedSchema, a loading UiButton, and a useSonner toast. The CLI is used to add the components.
expectations: Uses UiVee* wrapper components (for example UiVeeInput, UiVeeSelect, UiVeeCheckbox or UiVeeSwitch) for the fields instead of raw UiInput or native inputs with hand-written error markup
Every field has a name and a label, and the names match the keys of the validation schema
Uses useForm with validationSchema: toTypedSchema(schema) and binds handleSubmit to the form's @submit
Does not render separate error elements (such as a p with v-if on errors); relies on the field wrapper's built-in error message
Disables the fields while submitting (fieldset :disabled or equivalent) and sets :loading on the submit UiButton
Calls useSonner (for example useSonner.success) after saving and does not destructure it
Uses UiVeeSelect with native option children (not an options prop) if it uses UiVeeSelect
Installs the components with `ui-thing add ...` passing explicit names, and does not hand-write the components or run `ui-thing add` with no names
Does not import Ui* components, useForm, toTypedSchema or useSonner manually (Nuxt auto-imports them)
Uses no raw color classes such as bg-white, text-gray-500 or text-red-500

evals.prompt: I'm working in a Nuxt 4 project that already has UI Thing initialized (ui-thing.config.ts, components in app/components/Ui). Create a landing page for a project-management SaaS called 'Tasklane': hero, social proof, features, pricing, FAQ and footer.
evals.expected_output: A page assembled from UI Thing blocks (one per section) inside a consistent layout, with placeholder content replaced, found via plan-page/list-blocks or the docs, not hand-built sections.
expectations: Starts from UI Thing blocks for the hero, features, pricing, FAQ and footer sections (chosen with `ui-thing block --json --category <name>`, MCP plan-page / list-blocks, or the blocks docs, and added with `ui-thing block <names> --yes`) instead of hand-writing those sections from scratch
Uses one block per section and keeps a consistent tone, rather than mixing many unrelated styles for the same section
Installs the components and packages the chosen blocks need in one step (for example via get-install-plan or by checking each block's components) and registers any Nuxt modules they require
Replaces placeholder copy, # links and the COMPANY_NAME constant with content for Tasklane; no lorem ipsum or generic template text is left
Uses NuxtLink for internal links and adds useSeoMeta with a title and description
Uses semantic tokens (bg-background, text-muted-foreground, text-primary) and UiContainer for page width, with no raw colors or hand-rolled max-w-7xl mx-auto wrappers
Has at most one default-variant primary UiButton per section/view; secondary actions use outline or ghost
Checks the result in light and dark mode and at 375px width, or says it needs to be checked

evals.prompt: I'm working in a Nuxt 4 project that already has UI Thing initialized (ui-thing.config.ts, components in app/components/Ui). Add a 'Delete project' button on the project page. Clicking it should ask the user to confirm, then delete the project and show a success message.
evals.expected_output: A UiAlertDialog confirmation with the trigger rendered via as-child, a destructive action, and a useSonner toast.
expectations: Uses UiAlertDialog (with UiAlertDialogTrigger, UiAlertDialogContent, UiAlertDialogCancel and UiAlertDialogAction or the shortcut props the component documents) for the confirmation instead of window.confirm or a hand-built modal
Renders the trigger with as-child so there is no button nested inside a button
The confirm dialog has a title and a description
The destructive button uses variant="destructive" (or the destructive styling the action supports), not custom red classes
Shows a success toast with useSonner.success after the delete completes
Handles failure (an error toast or UiAlert) and keeps the user on the page
Does not use manual imports for Ui* components

evals.prompt: Set up a brand new Nuxt app called 'orbit' with UI Thing and add a button, card and input. I'm using bun. You can't answer interactive terminal prompts.
evals.expected_output: Non-interactive commands only: nuxi init with --template, bun install, ui-thing init --yes, ui-thing add with explicit names and --yes, with TypeScript 6 respected.
expectations: Creates the project with `nuxi init` passing --template (for example --template minimal) so it does not exit in a non-interactive terminal
Runs `ui-thing init --yes` (not plain `ui-thing init`) so no prompts are shown
Runs `ui-thing add button card input` with explicit component names (and --yes), not `ui-thing add` with no names
Uses bun (or bunx) consistently and does not create or leave a package-lock.json
Does not run `ui-thing prettier` or `ui-thing shortcuts` unattended (they prompt); if it adds blocks it passes block names and --yes (`ui-thing block BlockHero1 --yes`), never bare `ui-thing block`
Does not install TypeScript 7; if the build fails with 'No fs option provided to compileScript' it installs typescript@^6
Reads or checks ui-thing.config.ts and lists the components folder before assuming what is installed

evals.prompt: I'm working in a Nuxt 4 project that already has UI Thing initialized (ui-thing.config.ts, components in app/components/Ui). I want the glass-liquid effect from https://nxui.geoql.in/docs/components/fluid-glass on my pricing page hero. Don't convert it by hand.
evals.expected_output: Installs the component with ui-thing add from the nxui registry, then reviews the result: component name, SSR, dependencies, cn helper, and placeholder content.
expectations: Installs it with `ui-thing add` using the registry (`@nxui/fluid-glass` or https://nxui.geoql.in/r/fluid-glass.json) instead of rewriting the component by hand
Reads the file and package list the CLI prints (or passes --yes only after reviewing what the item is) because registry items are remote code
Checks the exact component name after install (for example in .nuxt/components.d.ts after nuxi prepare) instead of guessing the tag
Wraps the WebGL/canvas component in <ClientOnly> (or uses a .client.vue variant) to avoid SSR errors
Confirms the dependencies were installed (for example @vueuse/core, clsx) and that ~/lib/utils exports cn
Notices and resolves the duplicate component name warning (NUXT_B3011) caused by the item's index.ts barrel if it appears, for example by deleting the unused barrel
Uses it sparingly (one effect) and keeps text on top readable, with semantic tokens for the surrounding content

evals.prompt:
Convert this shadcn/ui React component to Vue for my UI Thing project:

```tsx
'use client'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { toast } from 'sonner'
import { Plus } from 'lucide-react'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger } from '@/components/ui/dialog'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'

export function NewProject() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [name, setName] = useState('')
  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <DialogTrigger asChild>
        <Button><Plus className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" />New project</Button>
      </DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader><DialogTitle>New project</DialogTitle></DialogHeader>
        <Input value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} placeholder="Name" />
        <Button onClick={() => { toast.success('Created'); setOpen(false) }}>Create</Button>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  )
}
```
evals.expected_output: A Vue SFC using UiDialog with v-model:open, as-child trigger, UiDialogContent shortcut props, the Icon component and useSonner.
expectations: Uses UiDialog with v-model:open instead of open/onOpenChange props
Uses UiDialogTrigger with as-child (not asChild)
Uses UiDialogContent with the title prop (or the title slot) and ensures a dialog title exists
Uses UiButton with the icon prop or the Icon component with lucide:plus, not an imported lucide-react component
Uses ref and v-model for the input state instead of useState/onChange
Uses useSonner.success (or useSonner) instead of importing toast from sonner, and mentions rendering <UiSonner /> once in app.vue
Removes 'use client', className, cn() and the @/components/ui/* imports; uses class and auto-imported Ui* components
Writes a Vue SFC with <script setup lang="ts">

evals.prompt: I'm working in a Nuxt 4 project that already has UI Thing initialized (ui-thing.config.ts, components in app/components/Ui). Build a 'Projects' list page that loads projects from /api/projects. Handle the loading state, an empty list, and a failed request.
evals.expected_output: A page with UiSkeleton loading placeholders, a UiEmpty empty state with a call to action, and a UiAlert (destructive) error with a retry.
expectations: Shows UiSkeleton placeholders shaped like the final rows while loading, not just a text 'Loading...'
Uses UiEmpty with its parts (for example UiEmptyHeader, UiEmptyTitle, UiEmptyDescription, UiEmptyContent) and a clear next action instead of a hand-styled div
Shows the error with UiAlert variant="destructive" (with a title and description) and offers a retry
Fetches data with useFetch or useAsyncData and uses its pending/error/status state
Uses semantic tokens only; no raw colors like text-gray-500 or bg-red-100
Uses UiBadge with variant and color for status values instead of hand-colored spans
Icon-only controls (such as row actions) have aria-label, preferably with a UiTooltip

evals.prompt: I'm working in a Nuxt 4 project that already has UI Thing initialized (ui-thing.config.ts, components in app/components/Ui). Add a revenue-over-time chart and a sortable, filterable, paginated customers table to the dashboard page.
evals.expected_output: UiApexchart rendered client-side and UiTanStackTable (or UiDatatable) for the table, using the right component names and client-only handling.
expectations: Uses UiApexchart (not UiApexcharts or a hand-rolled chart) for the chart and makes sure it renders client-side (<ClientOnly> or the .client component)
Uses UiTanStackTable or UiDatatable for the sortable, filterable, paginated table instead of a hand-written table with custom sorting code

Installs them with `ui-thing add` using the exact registry values (apexcharts and tanstacktable, found via ui-thing list, resolve-library-item or the components API) and lets the CLI install their packages (apexcharts, vue3-apexcharts, @tanstack/vue-table) instead of guessing names like tan-stack-table
Reads the component docs (get-component, /raw/components/<name>.md, or the apex-charts docs) for exact props instead of guessing them
Chart colors come from tokens (such as the chart-1..5 variables or text-primary), not hardcoded hex colors that ignore dark mode
Provides an empty state and a loading state for both the chart and the table

evals.prompt: I'm working in a Nuxt 4 project that already has UI Thing initialized (ui-thing.config.ts, components in app/components/Ui). Make the brand color a deep teal, add a 'success' color for positive states, and keep dark mode working.
evals.expected_output: Token changes in the Tailwind CSS file (and the theme command if appropriate), with success defined in :root, html.dark and @theme inline.
expectations: Changes colors through CSS variables in the Tailwind CSS file (tailwindCSSLocation), not by adding raw color classes to components
Defines the new success token in :root and in html.dark, and maps it in an @theme inline block (--color-success: var(--success)), with a matching success-foreground
Updates --primary (and --primary-foreground) in both :root and html.dark with readable contrast
If it uses `ui-thing theme`, passes the theme name and --yes, runs it before customizing tokens, and knows it overwrites the whole CSS file
Uses the new tokens (bg-success, text-success-foreground) or UiBadge color="green" in components instead of hardcoded greens
Does not add dark: overrides for tokens that already switch between modes

evals.prompt: Add a Callout and a Steps component to my Nuxt Content docs site using `ui-thing prose`.
evals.expected_output: Explains that ui-thing has no prose command and that these prose components ship with the @baybreezy/docd layer, instead of running a nonexistent command.
expectations: Does not run or recommend `ui-thing prose` and states the command does not exist
Points to the @baybreezy/docd Nuxt layer (for example `npx create-docd` or extending the layer) as the source of prose components such as callouts and steps
Does not invent other CLI commands (such as `ui-thing info` or `ui-thing docs`) to get the components
Mentions the MDC usage syntax (::prose-callout and ::prose-steps / ::prose-step) or points to the docd docs for it

evals.prompt: I'm editing the UI Thing source repository itself. I changed the props of app/components/Ui/Badge.vue and want the docs, MCP data and API to reflect it.
evals.expected_output: Follows the maintainer workflow from AGENTS.md: update source and docs demos, regenerate registries with the generator scripts, and format with oxfmt.
expectations: Reads AGENTS.md and the skill's maintainers/ notes before editing
Does not hand-edit generated files (server/utils/comp.ts, server/utils/block-examples.ts, app/utils/block-components.ts)
Regenerates the registries with `bun run generate:components` (or generate:all) after the change
Updates the docs demo SFC under app/components/content/Docs/** and lets automd keep the markdown snippets aligned, instead of pasting stale code into the markdown
Formats with oxfmt (`bun run fmt`) and does not run prettier on this repo
Keeps tv(), data-slot attributes, the class prop normalization (normalizeClass(props.class) || undefined) and Reka accessibility behavior intact

evals.prompt: I'm working in a Nuxt 4 project that already has UI Thing initialized (ui-thing.config.ts, components in app/components/Ui). Add a 'Share' icon button next to the page title that opens a menu with Copy link, Email and Download as PDF.
evals.expected_output: An accessible icon-only trigger with an aria-label and tooltip, a UiDropdownMenu with items, using Icon names from lucide.
expectations: Uses UiDropdownMenu (with its trigger rendered via as-child) and UiDropdownMenuItem for the menu instead of a hand-built popover with divs
The icon-only trigger button has an aria-label and preferably a UiTooltip
Uses Icon with lucide:* names (or the icon prop) and does not mix icon families or import icon components from an icon package
Sizes icons with size-* classes and does not nest a button inside a button
Copy link gives feedback with useSonner (for example useSonner.success('Link copied'))
Uses semantic tokens and built-in variants (variant="ghost" size="icon") instead of custom colors or borders
